subject: Recap & ask: token unit targets + host price scouting
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@datafolio.io>, Kara Nguyen <kara.nguyen@datafolio.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T15:06:00Z
Subject: Recap & ask: token unit targets + host price scouting

Hi Samir / Kara —

Great to meet you both on the demo earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can get a tight pilot proposal in front of procurement: 

1) Workload & volume checkpoints (you confirmed on call):
   - Primary workload: customer support triage + short-form generation (avg input+output ~ 120 tokens per request).
   - Expected steady-state monthly volume: 12M tokens / month (with spiky days up to 1.8M).
   - Embeddings for search + rerank: ~2M tokens / month (separate bucket).

2) Budget guidance you shared: $6k–$10k / month initially (you flagged flexibility if unit economics are compelling).

3) Immediate ask from our side: please confirm whether the budget range is firm (procurement target) or aspirational. We want to present 1–2 commercial options that hit your procurement target while preserving answer quality.

4) Quick price scouting vs hosts (high-level; model-specifics to follow):
   - OpenAI (latest instruct model): ~ $1,200 / 1M tokens (high-capacity generative).
   - Anthropic baseline: ~ $900 / 1M tokens.
   - Open-host competitor "HostX": ~ $650 / 1M tokens (quantized, single-region).
   - Redwood (suggested pilot): $700 / 1M tokens — quantized model with prefix/KV caching and burst pool.

Note: the numbers above are normalized to $/1M tokens for easy comparison — they depend heavily on model family, quantization, and caching assumptions. See attached spreadsheet for our assumptions and a quick model-by-model breakout.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm procurement target (firm vs aspirational) by EOD Friday.
- We prepare a 3-month pilot quote (cap + overage) and a mutual action plan (attached) for legal/procurement.
- If procurement needs an initial pilot discount, we can structure a capped pilot at a blended $/1M token rate.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a short note to Ben/Laura internally to lock the assumptions.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: datafolio_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (Excel stub), pricing-models-compare.csv (CSV stub)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@datafolio.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Kara Nguyen <kara.nguyen@datafolio.io>
Date: 2028-03-15T16:11:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap & ask: token unit targets + host price scouting

Jordan —

Thanks for the tidy recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Budget: $6k–$10k is the current procurement target. At RFP time we may stretch if the business case is clear, but procurement will push for something inside that band. So treat it as effectively a gating band for initial commercials.

- Volumes: the 12M estimate is conservative; we have growth scenarios where this ramps to ~35M over 6 months if pilot metrics hit. We will need both a pilot price and a scalable commercial price.

- Embeddings: yes, embeddings are required and should be priced separately (we will need both embedding and generative token rates).

Also — can you send the exact assumptions that produce the $700 / 1M Redwood number? Specifically: model variant, quantization level, expected cache hit rate, and whether rounding includes embedding tokens. Kara has procurement questions on caps and overage mechanics.

Appreciate it — I’ll loop procurement after we get the pilot quote.

Regards,
Samir Patel
Head of Data Products | DataFolio
samir.patel@datafolio.io

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T17:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Recap & ask: token unit targets + host price scouting — assumptions for $700 target

Ben / Laura —

Forwarding Samir's reply. They are firming procurement at $6k–$10k and potentially scale to 35M tokens in 6 months. They require separate embedding pricing. Procurement will want a pilot cap + overage terms.

Below I’m dropping the internal assumptions that justify listing $700 / 1M as our suggested pilot rate — these are conservative, intentionally favorable to DataFolio to win the pilot but still preserve margin: 

Assumptions (calculation basis):
- Model variant: quantized 16-bit derivative of the open LLM they prefer (equivalent generations per token ~ baseline LLM).
- Effective throughput: 60 tokens/sec per GPU on average during burst; continuous batching in prod yields 4x efficiency vs single-request baseline.
- Cache hit/prefix reuse: expected 18% effective token savings on average due to repeated prompts/patterns.
- GPU cost (cloud amortized, infra + ops): $2.80 / GPU-hour (after reserved capacity mix).
- Avg payload tokens per request: 120 tokens; tokens counted both in/out.

Quick back-of-envelope unit-econ: 
- Tokens per GPU-hour = throughput * seconds * efficiency multiplier = 60 tks/sec * 3600 sec * 4 = 864,000 tokens/hour.
- GPU cost per 1M tokens = ($2.80 / hour) * (1,000,000 / 864,000) = $3.24 (raw GPU compute) — note this is the compute-only floor.
- Add ops, storage, routing, infra delta, support & margin => multiply by factor ~ 35–200x depending on model family and NRE spread. For quantized open models with caching we use a conservative multiplier of 200x to arrive at a commercially viable $/1M.
- Commercialized $/1M = $3.24 * 200 ≈ $648 -> rounded to $700 for pilot packaging (includes embedding additive fee).

Rationale for multiplier: includes sustained infra overhead, infrequent model refresh NRE, customer support SLA, and business margin target to allow future discounts on scale. We can break this down line-by-line in the pricing spreadsheet.

Proposed pilot packaging options to discuss with procurement: 
A) 3-month pilot: up to 20M tokens total cap, blended $700 / 1M (embeddings at $250 / 1M). Overage billed monthly at the same blended rate.
B) 1-month POC: up to 5M tokens, $650 / 1M (conditional on immediate commit to a 3-month plan if metrics look good).
C) Volume-tiered commercial: 0–50M: $700 / 1M; 50–200M: $620 / 1M; 200M+: custom enterprise pricing.

Attachments: updated pricing-models-compare.csv (I populated it with the throughput math above and competitor normalized $/1M). I also drafted a mutual action plan that mirrors our standard pilot terms.

Two asks:
- Ben: can you validate the multiplier bands (is 200x defensible in our comps?)
- Laura: if procurement pushes hard on the $6k floor, do we offer a lower entry price (say $600 / 1M) tied to a 6-month minimum?

Thanks — I’ll wait for internal confirmation before sending the formal pilot quote.

Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T18:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap & ask: token unit targets + host price scouting — assumptions for $700 target

Jordan / Laura —

Quick take: 200x multiplier is on the high side but defensible for early pilots where we absorb some NRE. We should be prepared to offer a promotional entry price at $600 / 1M for the first month (cap 5M) to lock the pilot and then transition to the $700 blended rate for months 2–3. Embeddings at $250 / 1M is OK as a starting point.

If Samir confirms procurement is firm at $6k–$10k, offer A + promotional month and include a clause: if they hit >35M within 6 months we automatically move them to the volume-tiered commercial schedule and rebate a portion of pilot overage (simple credit).

I’ll draft a quick one-pager for procurement language and loop LA for legal redlines.
